summary: In this excerpt from Book 15 (part 140) of a fiction work, Ray is shown around Whiston's facilities by Emma and Amah, who explain the Trust's educational program for orphans bound for the colony of New Holyoke. Amah says the children are taught skills and social norms to assimilate, and that the colony embraces them in return for their contributions. Ray, embarrassed after questioning the children's emotional well-being, offers polite pleasantries and is relieved to avoid further trouble with the Whiston.
one_line: Ray is shown the Whiston's orphan education program, where Amah explains how the Trust prepares children for life on New Holyoke.
key_facts: Amah explains that the children in the Trust have great potential, and the Trust looks for that potential and helps them develop it.
Amah says the Trust attempts to give the children the facsimile of family as they go along.
Amah states that the Trust has only a short time to introduce the children to the type of lives they will lead on New Holyoke.
Amah says Blackheath Grange has better facilities and a large staff to continue the process of preparing the children.
Ray says that losing your parents is a pretty big blow to try to bounce back from.
Amah says that for some children, others have been without parents, comforts, and love for several years, and those cases take longer for the colony to embrace them.
Amah says the children receive love, friendship, support, and an extended family in return for becoming attractive members of the colony.
Amah asks Ray whether the arrangement is good for both sides, and Ray is not sure he agrees in principle.
Emma would like to show Ray the city, according to Amah, and some true Whiston hospitality would erase the harm.
Ray says he was a little surprised by the curriculum, which Amah says is quite advanced.
Ray says he didn't intend to sound critical.
Amah says some children lag significantly behind the educational level they should have attained.
The colony in question is New Holyoke.
